body.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and an admissible \(B\) in the sense of the graphical replacement lemma. Does the replacement graphical specification admit finite-alphabet shared-response-function kernels with positive selection probability and non-target kernel stability such that every pooled selected law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), \(k\in[K]\), is faithful to its replacement MAG? For any supplied finite-dimensional rational parameterization satisfying the Markov direction, this existence question reduces to atomic determinant nontriviality: for every \(k\in[K]\) and every conditional-independence query that is \(m\)-connected in the replacement MAG, at least one cleared conditional-independence determinant must be a nonzero polynomial on the equality-constrained shared-response-function parameter space. The finite-union exceptional-set argument is valid once these atomic certificates are available; the atomic certificates themselves remain open.
body.justification: This open question isolates faithful promotion from the exact graphical theorem; the established algebraic result applies only after a suitable rational shared-response parameterization and atomic determinant certificates are supplied.
body.gap: Both the nonempty open equality-constrained parameterization for an arbitrary replacement and determinant nontriviality for each \(m\)-connected query remain open.
body.consumer: An affirmative result would promote the two graphical endpoint constructions to faithful law-level witnesses, but would not by itself solve unknown-\(A\) completeness.

obligation.what_is_open: For every admissible replacement specification, first construct a nonempty open rational parameterization of one equality-constrained shared-exogenous shared-response twin-SCM family satisfying the Markov direction; then, for every query that is \(m\)-connected in a replacement MAG, exhibit a parameter point at which at least one cleared conditional-independence determinant is nonzero.
obligation.obstruction: Generic faithfulness for unrestricted multinomial DAGs does not imply polynomial nontriviality after non-target response equalities, a common basal selection event, shared exogenous variables, and fixed one-half pooled weights are imposed. The frozen core supplies neither the required parameter-space construction nor a cross-world coupling that witnesses each atomic dependence.
obligation.attempted: Used the established exceptional-set reduction to isolate all unfaithfulness events as finitely many determinant zero sets and the product-polynomial argument to obtain one simultaneous point once atomic nontriviality holds. This route cannot prove that the equality-constrained parameter space is nonempty and open for every replacement or that no required determinant vanishes identically on it.
obligation.partial_result: For any supplied nonempty open set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^r\) that rationally parameterizes equality-constrained shared-response-function models, has strictly positive cells and denominators, and satisfies the Markov direction, conditional independence is equivalent to finitely many cleared determinant-polynomial equations. For each \(m\)-connected query choose one determinant polynomial \(q_i\) that is not identically zero. Because \(\Theta\) is nonempty and open and \(\prod_i q_i\) is a nonzero polynomial, some \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) satisfies \(\prod_i q_i(\theta^\star)\ne0\). At this common point all pooled selected laws are simultaneously faithful. Conversely, any simultaneously faithful point makes at least one determinant for each \(m\)-connected query nonzero and hence certifies its nontriviality. Positive local tables provide factorization, non-target response stability, and positive selection. What remains unproved is both the construction of a suitable nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization for every replacement specification and the atomic nontriviality certificate on that constrained parameter space.
